Electronics i made for a large LED clock. (sic)

• The red chip to the left is a DS3234 real time clock and its job is to keep time to a very high degree of accuracy and it has his back-up battery below him.

  • The black chips on the top are TLC5940 led drivers that power up to 16 leds each and they have their current limiting resistors.

  • The knobs and buttons to the right control things like setting the time, brightness and there is also a light sensor for automatic brightness control.

  • Upper left corner is the power regulator with a large heatsink.

  • The white chip in the middle is an ATmega 168 8bit controller running Arduino code. Actually its what the Arduino UNO basically consists of in a minimal form. That is the brains of the operation that ties everything together.

As for the actual display part...I'm not gonna picture that for some privacy reasons that could pop up in future, but I'll tell you: if you can imagine it, it can power it.

Two examples of other peoples clock for reference: https://kek.gg/i/3YsGtv.jpeg ----- https://kek.gg/i/gHmgR.jpeg
